stories.headline: Samsung deploys ChatGPT Enterprise and Codex to Korea staff and global DX division

key_facts.fact: OpenAI announced Samsung Electronics is deploying ChatGPT Enterprise and Codex to all employees in South Korea and to all workers worldwide in its Device eXperience (DX) division.
key_facts.excerpt: ChatGPT Enterprise and Codex available to all Samsung Electronics employees in Korea and all Device eXperience (DX) employees worldwide. Samsung's global deployment is one of OpenAI's largest enterprise launches ever.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI described the rollout as one of its largest enterprise deployments to date, spanning R&D, manufacturing, marketing and corporate functions.
key_facts.excerpt: Samsung Electronics to use ChatGPT and Codex across its operations, from R&D and manufacturing to marketing, corporate functions, and other areas of its business.

key_facts.fact: More than 5 million people use Codex every week, and weekly active Codex users in South Korea have risen nearly 800% since February 1, 2026, per OpenAI.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI said more than 5 million people use Codex every week for technical and non-technical work. Weekly active Codex users in South Korea have risen by nearly 800 percent since Feb. 1, 2026.

key_facts.fact: The rollout reverses a 2023 Samsung company-wide ban on ChatGPT, imposed after employees leaked proprietary source code via the chatbot.
key_facts.excerpt: This rollout signifies a shift for Samsung, which previously banned generative AI tools in 2023 after employees leaked proprietary code using ChatGPT.

key_facts.fact: The agreement extends an existing collaboration on AI infrastructure; the two firms signed a letter of intent last October for Samsung to supply advanced memory for OpenAI's next-generation systems.
key_facts.excerpt: Samsung has been working with OpenAI on supplying advanced memory semiconductors, critical for next-generation AI systems, after the two parties signed a letter of intent last October.

key_facts.fact: Samsung's Device Solutions semiconductor division, previously using Anthropic's Claude, opened access to ChatGPT on June 12 as part of an 'AX' AI transformation initiative announced in early June 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: The deployment aligns with Samsung's 'AX' initiative, aimed at AI transformation and announced in early June 2026. As part of this strategy, the DX division began operations of three external generative AI services on June 12, 2026, which include OpenAI's ChatGPT, Google's Gemini Enterprise, and Anthropic's Claude.

stories.headline: Getty Images signs multi-year display deal with OpenAI to license images for ChatGPT

key_facts.fact: Getty Images Holdings (NYSE: GETY) announced a multi-year display agreement with OpenAI, putting its licensed image library into ChatGPT search and discovery experiences.
key_facts.excerpt: Getty Images (NYSE: GETY), a preeminent global visual content creator and marketplace, today announced a display agreement with OpenAI. Under the partnership Getty Images' licensed content libraries will appear across OpenAI search and discovery experiences within ChatGPT.

key_facts.fact: Getty CEO Craig Peters said high-quality licensed visual content makes AI-powered search 'more useful and more trustworthy'.
key_facts.excerpt: 'High-quality, licensed visual content makes AI-powered search and discovery more useful and more trustworthy. This partnership with OpenAI reflects a shared recognition of that, and together we will deliver richer visual experiences to ChatGPT users,' said Craig Peters, Chief Executive Officer at Getty Images.

key_facts.fact: The agreement covers display and attribution only; OpenAI is not permitted to use the images to train its models.
key_facts.excerpt: Here's the thing that makes this deal interesting: it's specifically about display and attribution, not about feeding images into OpenAI's training pipeline. In English, ChatGPT users will see Getty's rights-cleared photos in visual responses, with proper credit attached, but OpenAI doesn't get to use those images to make its AI models smarter.

key_facts.fact: GETY shares recently traded near $0.61, close to the lower end of their 52-week range of about $0.58 to $3.21, when the deal was announced.
key_facts.excerpt: GETY shares recently traded near $0.61, close to the lower end of their 52-week range of about $0.58 to $3.21, making the announcement strategically meaningful but not yet enough to erase market skepticism.

stories.headline: Tencent tests Xiaowei AI assistant inside WeChat, using WeLM and DeepSeek models

key_facts.fact: Tencent has started testing a new AI assistant for WeChat called Xiaowei, available to a small set of users from June 22, 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: Tencent Holdings Ltd. has started testing a new AI assistant for WeChat as part of its efforts to catch up with peers in China's white-hot artificial intelligence race. Known as Weixin in China, the super app has made the new AI assistant available to a small number of users.

key_facts.fact: Xiaowei primarily runs on Weixin's own large language model WeLM, while routing some queries to DeepSeek, per Tencent's customer service unit.
key_facts.excerpt: Xiaowei mainly uses Weixin's own large language model WeLM while sometimes turning to DeepSeek to process some queries, Tencent's customer service unit said in a separate statement.

key_facts.fact: Users interact with Xiaowei via text or voice; it can adjust settings, send messages, hail rides, order food and generate images by tapping WeChat's mini-app ecosystem.
key_facts.excerpt: Users can interact with the AI agent, called 'Xiaowei', via text or voice, and complete tasks by tapping into mini apps. The agent assists with a wide range of tasks, including changing settings, sending messages, ordering food, hailing rides and generating images.

key_facts.fact: WeChat (Weixin in China) has roughly 1.4 billion users, and Tencent currently trails ByteDance and Alibaba in user adoption and frontier model development.
key_facts.excerpt: WeChat is China's most popular messaging platform with roughly 1.4bn users.

key_facts.fact: Tencent already has a separate WeChat-embedded chatbot called Yuanbao; reporting says Xiaowei has been made the company's highest strategic priority despite high rollout costs.
key_facts.excerpt: The publication reported that the company made the AI agent roll-out its highest strategic priority, while internal estimates suggest that a full roll out of Xiaowei will be very costly for the company. Tencent itself already has an embedded chatbot in WeChat called Yuanbao.

key_facts.fact: Tencent reportedly led the recent $7.4B fundraising round into DeepSeek and is said to have proposed taking a 20% stake in the startup.
key_facts.excerpt: Tencent is closely associated with DeepSeek, which reportedly led the recent $7.4bn round into the AI start-up. The company was also reported to have proposed taking a 20pc stake in the start-up.

stories.headline: SoftBank-backed embodied AI robotics firm Coowa plans Hong Kong IPO at $3B+ valuation

key_facts.fact: Shanghai-based Coowa is preparing to file a Hong Kong IPO application within the next two to three months, with Huatai Securities and Deutsche Bank advising.
key_facts.excerpt: SoftBank-backed Coowa is preparing to seek a Hong Kong listing after raising more than US$600 million (approx. $836.4 million) in its latest funding round, the Wall Street Journal reported, citing people familiar with the matter. Huatai Securities and Deutsche Bank are advising Coowa on the listing, according to the Wall Street Journal.

key_facts.fact: Coowa's latest funding round raised over $600 million and pushed its valuation above $3 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: Backed by SoftBank Group, Coowa has raised over $600 million in its latest funding round, pushing its valuation to over $3 billion.

key_facts.fact: The company has deployed more than 10,000 robots across more than 50 cities and regions, and generated more than 1 billion yuan (~$147 million) in revenue in 2025.
key_facts.excerpt: The Shanghai-based company has deployed more than 10,000 robots across more than 50 cities and regions, generated more than 1 billion yuan in revenue in 2025, and is now valued at more than US$3 billion (approx. $4.2 billion).

key_facts.fact: Founded in 2015, Coowa started in autonomous driving and pivoted to 'embodied' physical AI; in May 2026 it released CooWAIM 2.0, described as the industry's first interactive world-action model.

key_facts.fact: Backers include SoftBank Group and the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank.

stories.headline: Nadella tells WSJ AI giants must earn 'societal permission' as Microsoft pushes lower-cost models

key_facts.fact: In a Wall Street Journal interview published June 21, 2026, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella directly criticized OpenAI and Anthropic by name as 'emblematic' of an industry structured around a few dominant models.
key_facts.excerpt: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella delivered the sharpest public rebuke yet of the company's two most important financial partners — OpenAI and Anthropic — arguing that an industry structured around a handful of dominant AI models is not just economically dangerous but politically unsustainable... Nadella pointed specifically at OpenAI and Anthropic — companies in which Microsoft has invested billions — as emblematic of an approach that prioritizes model dominance over the broader economy's right to benefit from AI.

key_facts.fact: Nadella said: 'You can't say, hey, all white-collar jobs are gone and this could even be a weapon and we will use all the power to build data centers.'
key_facts.excerpt: 'You can't say, hey, all white-collar jobs are gone and this could even be a weapon and we will use all the power to build data centers,' Nadella told the Wall Street Journal.

key_facts.fact: Microsoft is weighing hosting a version of the low-cost Chinese DeepSeek model, despite Anthropic and OpenAI alleging that DeepSeek distilled their top models.
key_facts.excerpt: The WSJ report stated that Microsoft is weighing an option to host a version of the low-cost Chinese model DeepSeek, as an effort to drive prices down for using AI, though Anthropic and OpenAI have alleged the former for distilling or stealing their top models.

key_facts.fact: Microsoft has rolled out a suite of low-cost models and released Copilot Cowork, an autonomous agent that lets users choose between AI models for long-running tasks.
key_facts.excerpt: In a matter of weeks, Microsoft has rolled out a suite of low-cost models meant to drive prices down for customers bracing from the sticker shock of skyrocketing AI bills. The company released Copilot Cowork, an autonomous AI 'agent' allowing users to choose various AI models, including cheaper ones, as they complete long-running tasks.

key_facts.fact: The interview escalates an essay Nadella posted on X on June 14, 2026, titled 'A frontier without an ecosystem is not stable', which Tech Times says reached more than 60 million views.
key_facts.excerpt: The Wall Street Journal interview escalates what Nadella began seven days earlier in a personal essay posted to X on June 14, titled 'A frontier without an ecosystem is not stable.' That essay reached more than 60 million views.

key_facts.fact: Nadella told the WSJ: 'No amount of just narrative is going to do it because where we are now, we have to sort of walk the walk... We now have to do the hard work in earning the social permission.'
key_facts.excerpt: 'No amount of just narrative is going to do it because where we are now, we have to sort of walk the walk,' Nadella said, pointing out the need to ensure people feel like they have agency and economic opportunity. 'We now have to do the hard work in earning the social permission.'

stories.headline: Defense tech startups raise $12.3B in 2026 H1, already topping all of 2025 — PitchBook

key_facts.fact: Defense technology startups raised $12.3 billion globally from venture capital in the first half of 2026, already surpassing the $9.95 billion raised across all of 2025, according to PitchBook data cited by the Financial Times on June 21.
key_facts.excerpt: According to the British Financial Times (FT) and global market research firm PitchBook on the 22nd (local time), defense technology startups worldwide have raised $12.3 billion (approximately 18.8 trillion Korean won) from VCs so far this year. This is nearly double the amount raised during the same period last year and has already surpassed the total investment of $9.95 billion recorded for the entire previous year.

key_facts.fact: US-based startups captured $11.4 billion of the $12.3 billion total — about 93% — with Anduril Industries alone taking nearly half of US funding.
key_facts.excerpt: According to PitchBook data, American startups secured $11.4 billion, or 93% of the total $12.3 billion in defense technology investments during the first half of this year. Nearly half of this amount was claimed by Anduril Industry.

key_facts.fact: Anduril raised an additional $5 billion last month, nearly doubling its valuation to $61 billion within a year.
key_facts.excerpt: The company raised an additional $5 billion last month, nearly doubling its enterprise value to $61 billion within a year.

key_facts.fact: German defense AI startup Helsing is raising $1.2 billion at a valuation of about $18 billion, and Germany's STARK is in talks for at least €300 million.
key_facts.excerpt: FT reported that Helsing was raising $1.2 billion at a valuation of approximately $18 billion. Another German defense company, STARK, is also in talks to raise at least 300 million euros.

key_facts.fact: Investor focus has shifted from aerial drones (described as crowded) toward autonomous maritime systems, military satellites, electronic warfare and battlefield AI.
key_facts.excerpt: Experts say the drone sector shows signs of overcrowding, but autonomous maritime systems, military satellites and battlefield AI remain in the early stages of growth. 'If the first wave of investment was about restoring weapons production capacity, we are now moving into a race to secure supply chains and advanced technology,' said Mikolaj Firlej... 'Sensors, electronic warfare and battlefield AI will be the core investment areas for years to come.'

stories.headline: MiniMax releases M2.1, claiming it tops Claude Sonnet 4.5 on multilingual coding

key_facts.fact: MiniMax released MiniMax-M2.1 on June 22, 2026, an update to its M2 model focused on multilingual programming and complex real-world tasks.
key_facts.excerpt: Today we are releasing updates to the model component, namely MiniMax M2.1, hoping to help more enterprises and individuals find more AI-native ways of working (and living) sooner.

key_facts.fact: MiniMax says M2.1 delivers a significant leap over M2 on core software-engineering leaderboards and 'outperforms Claude Sonnet 4.5 and closely approaches Claude Opus 4.5' in multilingual scenarios.
key_facts.excerpt: MiniMax-M2.1 delivers a significant leap over M2 on core software engineering leaderboards. It shines particularly bright in multilingual scenarios, where it outperforms Claude Sonnet 4.5 and closely approaches Claude Opus 4.5.

key_facts.fact: The model was evaluated on SWE-bench Verified across a variety of coding agent frameworks, which MiniMax says demonstrate 'exceptional framework generalization and robust stability'.
key_facts.excerpt: We also evaluated MiniMax-M2.1 on SWE-bench Verified across a variety of coding agent frameworks. The results highlight the model's exceptional framework generalization and robust stability.

key_facts.fact: MiniMax also introduced a new benchmark called VIBE (Visual & Interactive Benchmark for Execution) with five subsets — Web, Simulation, Android, iOS, Backend — using an 'Agent-as-a-Verifier' paradigm; M2.1 scored 88.6 average, with 91.5 on VIBE-Web and 89.7 on VIBE-Android.
key_facts.excerpt: This suite encompasses five core subsets: Web, Simulation, Android, iOS, and Backend. Distinguishing itself from traditional benchmarks, VIBE leverages an innovative Agent-as-a-Verifier (AaaV) paradigm to automatically assess the interactive logic and visual aesthetics of generated applications within a real runtime environment. MiniMax-M2.1 delivers outstanding performance on the VIBE aggregate benchmark, achieving an average score of 88.6—demonstrating robust full-stack development capabilities. It excels particularly in the VIBE-Web (91.5) and VIBE-Android (89.7) subsets.

sources.title: MiniMax M2.1: Significantly Enhanced Multi-Language Programming, Built for Real-World Complex Tasks
